charter:
# Charter — S21 Message Construction (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

- **Project:** S21 'Message construction (the compiled prompt)', track v1, ADM phase G, delivery plateau, tranche 9, plan `docs/plans/slices/S21-message-construction.md`.
- **Sponsor:** the programme's sponsoring group, through the tranche-9 PI plan and the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14.
- **Authority:** SPEC_V2 §3 D27 with §4.4, §4.5, §7.7, §10.2, §11.1 and §11.4 and the §8 S21 definition; the owner ruling of 2026-11-09 makes a prompt a run-time compilation from the procedure and the other system, tenant and project sources, stored in Postgres, not a 2024 template.
- **Objective:** every model call carries a compiled prompt the run selected for this step — procedure, capability/role, knowledge, memory, request and card sources in trust order — with the recipe pin and a 64-hex SHA-256 recorded, and a generated draft applying only through an accepted decision that names it.
- **Scope:** the `prompt`, `prompt_section`, `decision_option_set`, `decision_option_set_option` and `organisation_layer` tables; the `prompt_recipes.*`, `cards.assign`, `ladder.*`, `laya.classify`, `decision_options.*` and `organisation_layers.*` actions; the prompt, memory, knowledge and executor modules; eleven build steps, with all nine linked issues closed at the snapshot.
- **Acceptance:** the plan's §9 five criteria, carried per step by the suites and receipts the plan names and at project level by `acceptance/programme/S21.toml`.
- **Status:** the project stays active. This charter and the lifecycle set that follows are authored retrospectively for the tranche-9 rework; they record what the pinned snapshot holds and do not claim the product's build gate has been re-run for the pack.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — S21 Message Construction (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

body.assignment: The architecture work assigns S21 the compiled prompt as a product surface: a recipe with authored sections and budgets, a selector that chooses concrete sources per run, a pure compiler that renders them in trust order and hashes the text, an `internal_agent` executor that dispatches on the release anatomy and holds a closed tool grant, an L1 laya gate that makes its own call and records the exchange it verified, an L3 human gate that applies a draft, memory that carries the run's prior steps and the card's handoff note, and a release that compiles its knowledge layers or refuses. The statement is retrospective: it describes the assignment the plan set and the state the 2026-11-28 snapshot carries.
body.scope: In scope are the five tables and the migrations that add them (0030, 0031, 0032, 0062, 0071, 0074), the actions `prompt_recipes.create|list|get|activate|retire`, `cards.assign`, `ladder.prepare`, `laya.classify`, `ladder.evaluate`, `decision_options.*` and `organisation_layers.set|list`, the `prompts:read` and `prompts:write` scopes, and the prompt, memory, knowledge and executor modules across eleven build steps. Out of scope are a second prompt compiler or PDDL as storage (§6), the executor budget mechanism `v1-p75-1` (the #526 lane's), an external runtime, any UI, parent-run memory in a child's prompt, a claim/renew/release verb, and the programme record itself, which is #526's lane.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors this retrospective set under the standing delegation; the Architecture Board reviews the Phase A–D artefacts and the statement; the SRO is accountable for the capability and the tranche outcome; a tenant admin holds `prompts:write` and `jobs:write` to author recipes and release anatomy; the internal agent receives only the sources the selector chose and the tools the grant enables; and a person holding the approval decides the L3 gate, because the approval writer enforces `decided_by_kind = human`. The session that authored this pack is not the accepting role, so the separation of duties holds.
body.acceptance_criteria: The gate is the plan's §9 acceptance: a step whose recipe requires `procedure` and whose run has none fails by name before a model call; the same recipe and the same facts compile byte-identically, with hash equality as the test; changing a card changes the hash and changing an unrelated tenant's card does not; an over-budget section refuses with the measured size and never truncates, with `budget = measured` compiling and `measured - 1` refusing; and the prompt audit names the compiled text it audited by `(prompt_ref, prompt_sha256)`. Each build step adds its own named suites and receipt in §10–§23, and `acceptance/programme/S21.toml` is the manifest that carries the project-level acceptance.
body.contract: The contract commits to one compiler: `conveyor_domain::prompt::compile` renders every source, and `compile_for_run` resolves facts, memory and knowledge targets in one transaction, commits, then calls the one retrieval path with no transaction open. The compiled text is never stored; the provenance is the recipe pin (`prompt_ref`, `prompt_version`) and the SHA-256, which the `inference_call` row and the audit finding both carry. The executor is the one dispatch point keyed by `ExecutorKind`, the release snapshot is the execution authority and the live `capability_agent` row is the outer ceiling, and the model's surface is `bound_tools(run) ∩ enabled(grants) ∩ effect ≤ min(grant.max_side_effect, binding.effect_ceiling)`. The apply path is one `pub(crate)` helper shared with the resume worker, and `documents.update` stays closed to generated drafts.
body.retrospective: This statement is authored on 2026-11-28 for the tranche-9 rework. No contemporaneous statement of architecture work exists in the snapshot: the delivery was recorded in the slice plan, its eleven build records and the receipts `docs/evidence/S21-*.md`, and the project row stays active. The statement therefore records the terms the plan set, the decisions the records close (budgets in characters, the role from the binding, the plan projection on demand, park by default) and the open questions the plan leaves, rather than implying a ceremonial review that never happened.

# Solution Concept Diagram — S21 Message Construction (Phase A)

## Metadata

Type diagram; phase A; plateau psa; version 1; status draft; owner the programme architect (conveyor-e2e); reviewer the Architecture Board; review date 2026-11-28; project S21; tranche 9; retrospective under the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. Authored by the tranche-9 rework; it does not attest contemporaneous intent.

## Entries

The concept has eight parts. A recipe names section kinds and budgets; the selector chooses sources; `compile_for_run` resolves and commits before the one retrieval call and then compiles purely; the executor dispatches on the release anatomy and intersects the tool grant; the ladder builds, calls and verifies; the applying gate parks, decides and resumes; memory carries prior steps and the handoff note; and the release compiles its layers. The entries deliberately show the seams each build record defends, including the no-transaction retrieval and the human-only approval.

## Links

Realizes the Requirements Catalog; depends on the Business Capability Map and the Data Entity catalogue. The source is `docs/plans/slices/S21-message-construction.md` §4 and its §12, §14, §16, §18, §20–§23 build plans. The diagram is textual because the record's artefact action carries entries rather than an image.

## Document

The diagram keeps the boundary the plan draws: no PDDL as storage, no second compiler, no external runtime, and one dispatch point. It is published as an architecture-artifact-instance by the rework factory, and its point is that the selector, the compiler, the executor and the gate are the product, while the stored text does not exist.

# Architecture Artefact Index — S21 (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Metadata

The artefact set for S21 is the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts on the delivery track: the Stakeholder Map, the Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog, the Requirements Catalog and the Solution Concept Diagram at phase a, plateau psa; the Business Capability Map at phase b; the Data Entity/Data Component Catalog at phase c; and the Technology Standards Catalog at phase d. Each carries an authored body dated 2026-11-28; the owner is the programme architect under the tranche-9 rework delegation, the reviewer is the Architecture Board, and the subject is this project's record at the pinned snapshot.

## Entries

The set is seven rows in the order the standard seeds them: a/matrix — Stakeholder Map — S21 Message Construction (Phase A); a/catalog — Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog — S21 Message Construction (Phase A); a/catalog — Requirements Catalog — S21 Message Construction (Phase A); a/diagram — Solution Concept Diagram — S21 Message Construction (Phase A); b/diagram — Business Capability Map — S21 Message Construction (Phase B); c/catalog — Data Entity/Data Component Catalog — S21 Message Construction (Phase C); d/catalog — Technology Standards Catalog — S21 Message Construction (Phase D).

## Links

Every artefact links to another artefact of the set with one of the four kinds the record's link action allows: derivation, realization, reuse or dependency. The links follow the phase order, so a reader can walk from A to D without an orphan, and each artefact's own Links section names its source in the slice plan and the tree. The deepest source is `docs/plans/slices/S21-message-construction.md` §3–§5, §9 and §10–§23.

## Document

This index is published as its own architecture-artifact document by the rework factory. It is the document the close gate reads for the project's artefact standard, and it is why the set can be verified without re-reading the plan: the titles, the order and the link kinds are all stated here, and the seven rows match the seven artefacts one for one.

documents.body:
# Inception Analysis — S21 Message construction (retrospective, Phase G)

## Current state

Before S21 the message was a fixed five-section template: the prompt catalogue held a recipe and the pure renderer compiled it, but the run selected no sources, memory never reached the prompt, a generated draft could be attached without a decision that named it, and a release never compiled its knowledge layers. The slice plan records the seam as real — exact-pin resolution, a pure renderer and a recorded hash — and the work as eleven build steps that turn the compile into a selection and budget step over many candidate sources. At the 2026-11-28 snapshot the record measures the project built, all nine linked issues are closed, and the project row stays active in tranche 9.

## Reuse sources

The plan reuses S15's capability, capability_agent and capability_knowledge rows, S16's prompt audit, S13's `agent.run`, S11's procedure and step rows and S09's `retrieval.query` and `strata` packs, and inside this tree it reuses the prompt catalogue and pure renderer from the v1 seam, the T0 executor contract, the bound-tool projection and the existing approval, job and memory primitives rather than adding a parallel escalation or queue. Each reuse is a live row, action or module at the same snapshot, so the build extends a seam instead of forking one.

## Build vs reuse

The build side is the selector with kinds, limits and a deterministic order; the recipe CRUD surface with one draft and one active version per key; card-scoped memory selection with its ids inside the hash; the `internal_agent` executor and its closed tool grant; the applying gate with its parked run and resume worker; the declared request source; the handoff's one transaction; and the L1 laya gate that makes and verifies its own call. Refused by the plan: a second prompt compiler, PDDL as storage, an external runtime, a second retrieval path, a second apply path and the executor budget mechanism, which another lane already owns.

## Risks

Three risks are carried. A later unit could reconstruct a prompt in its own code and record a hash that covers a different text, which the one-compiler rule and the recorded `(prompt_ref, prompt_sha256)` pair are there to prevent. The live wire proof against the real inference-router and laya bridge is blocked on the estate's licensed caller, so the product's live evidence is absent while its suites are green. And tenant-authored recipes widen the authoring surface, with the compiler's trust sort and measured budget as the only invariants a tenant-authored version must still pass.

# Architecture Analysis — S21 Message construction (retrospective, Phase G)

## Current state

At the pinned snapshot the project carries five tables — `prompt`, `prompt_section`, `decision_option_set`, `decision_option_set_option` and `organisation_layer` — the recipe, handoff, ladder, option and organisation-layer action families, and the prompt, memory, knowledge and executor modules across eleven build steps. The plan's status is built, the nine linked issues are closed, and the record measures built; the project row stays active because its manifest declares no closure checks. The upstream seams the plan reads — the procedure, capability, knowledge, audit and retrieval surfaces — exist at the same snapshot.

## Options considered

Five choices were weighed. A fixed template against run-time selection: selection won, because a present but irrelevant section costs tokens and hides the fact that mattered. Storing the compiled text against storing only the pin and the SHA-256: hash-only won, so the prompt is not a second store to secure. A second retrieval path inside the compile transaction against one path called after the commit: the single path won. A caller-supplied laya verdict against an engine exchange the action verifies: verification won. And auto-applying an accepted draft against parking by default: park won, with the policy opting in.

## Risks

The same three risks the inception records recur here at architecture level: a second prompt surface drifting from the one compiler; the live proof blocked on a licensed caller and a reachable router and laya bridge; and tenant-authored recipes changing trust order or budget. The design answers each structurally — one renderer, one retrieval implementation, one dispatch map, one apply helper — but a review must still check that a new surface uses them rather than merely citing them. No risk is closed by prose.

## Dependency map

The slice plan's frontmatter declares seven upstream dependencies: S09 supplies retrieval and the strata packs the knowledge section queries; S11 the procedure and step rows the request renders; S13 the `agent.run` surface the executor extends; S15 the capability and knowledge tables; S16 the prompt audit that names the compiled text; and T2 and T13 the release and executor contract the runtime dispatches on. The project row records the same edges. The executor budget mechanism is outside every S21 step and arrives from another lane, and the live proof depends on the owner provisioning a licensed caller.

# Architecture Design — S21 Message construction (retrospective, Phase G)

## Context and boundary

The design places message construction at the run boundary: a recipe names section kinds and a character ceiling, a selector chooses concrete sources for this step, one compiler renders them in trust order and hashes the text, and the hash plus the recipe pin are the only record. In scope are the five tables and their migrations, the action families the plan lists, the prompt, memory, knowledge and executor modules, and the eleven build steps. Out of scope are a second compiler, PDDL as storage, an external runtime, a second retrieval or apply path, any UI, parent-run memory in a child's prompt, and the programme record itself.

## Aggregates, tables and actions

Five aggregates carry the design. `prompt` and `prompt_section` carry the versioned recipe with one draft and one active per tenant and key; `procedure_step.outputs` carries the declared dot-path outputs the plan projection checks; `decision_option_set` and its option rows carry the authored menu a choice-type policy is asked over; `organisation_layer` carries base, industry, department archetype, each department in declared order and the job; and the `inference_call` columns carry the call's identity. The actions are the recipe family, `cards.assign`, `ladder.prepare`, `laya.classify`, `ladder.evaluate`, the option and organisation-layer families, and `ladder.apply_draft` as the one apply path.

## Decisions

The recorded decisions are: budgets in characters, measured on the block as written, with `budget = measured` compiling and `measured - 1` refusing; the role from the capability binding rather than the run principal's scopes; the plan projection derived on demand and enforced at publish, never stored; park by default on an accepted draft, with the policy opting into apply; the prompt pin required for every active internal agent, so no model call runs without compiled text and a 64-hex hash; and the compiled text never stored, with source identities inside the hash's pre-image.

## Acceptance

The plan's §9 is the acceptance: a step whose recipe requires `procedure` and whose run has none fails by name before a model call; the same recipe and the same facts compile byte-identically, with hash equality as the test; changing the card moves the hash and changing an unrelated tenant's card does not; an over-budget section refuses with its measured size and never truncates; and the prompt audit names the compiled text it audited by `(prompt_ref, prompt_sha256)`. Each build step adds its own named suites and receipt, and the project-level acceptance is the manifest `acceptance/programme/S21.toml`.

## Architecture artefacts

The set is the seven mandatory Phase A–D artefacts at the delivery profile: the Stakeholder Map, the Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog, the Requirements Catalog and the Solution Concept Diagram at phase A; the Business Capability Map at phase B; the Data Entity/Data Component Catalog at phase C; and the Technology Standards Catalog at phase D, each with an authored body dated 2026-11-28 and linked to another artefact of the set. The Architecture Artefact Index documents their titles, order and link kinds, so the close gate can read one published document per category without re-reading the plan.

# Statement of Architecture Work — S21 Message construction (retrospective, Phase G)

## Assignment

The architecture work assigns S21 the compiled prompt as a product surface: a recipe with authored sections and a ceiling, a selector that chooses concrete sources per run, a pure compiler that renders them in trust order and hashes the text, an `internal_agent` executor that dispatches on a typed release anatomy under a closed tool grant, an L1 laya gate that makes its own call and records the exchange it verified, an L3 human gate that applies a draft, memory that carries the run's prior steps and the card's handoff note, and a release that compiles its knowledge layers or refuses. The statement is retrospective: it records the assignment the plan set and the state the 2026-11-28 snapshot carries.

## Scope

In scope are the five tables and the migrations that add them, the recipe, handoff, ladder, option and organisation-layer actions, the `prompts:read` and `prompts:write` scopes, and the prompt, memory, knowledge and executor modules across eleven build steps. Out of scope are a second prompt compiler, PDDL as storage, the executor budget mechanism the plan assigns to another lane, an external runtime, any UI, parent-run memory in a child's prompt, a claim or lane verb, and the programme record itself, which this pack does not own.

## Responsibilities

The programme architect authors this retrospective set under the standing delegation; the Architecture Board reviews the Phase A–D artefacts and the statement; the SRO is accountable for the capability and the tranche outcome; a tenant admin holds `prompts:write` and `jobs:write` to author recipes and release anatomy; the internal agent receives only the sources the selector chose and the tools the grant enables; and a person holding the approval decides the L3 gate, because the approval writer enforces `decided_by_kind = human`. The session that authored this pack is not the accepting role, so the separation of duties holds.

## Acceptance criteria

The gate is the plan's §9 acceptance: a required source refuses by name before a model call; equal facts compile byte-identically; the card moves the hash and another tenant's card does not; an over-budget section refuses with the measured size and never truncates; and the audit names `(prompt_ref, prompt_sha256)`. Each build step adds its named suites and its receipt, and the project-level manifest is `acceptance/programme/S21.toml`. The live proof is recorded as blocked on the licensed caller rather than counted as met.

## Contract

The contract commits to one compiler for every source, one retrieval path called with no transaction open, one executor dispatch keyed by `ExecutorKind`, one `pub(crate)` apply helper shared with the resume worker, the compiled text never stored, and the model's surface as the intersection of the run's bound tools, the enabled grants and both effect ceilings. It also commits to the recipe pin and the SHA-256 as the call's provenance and to `documents.update` staying closed to generated drafts. The project stays active; this contract does not close it.

# User stories — S21 Message construction (retrospective, Phase G)

## Personas

Four personas carry the stories: a tenant admin who authors prompt recipes and release anatomy under `prompts:write` and `jobs:write`; an internal agent that executes one step and must receive only the sources the selector chose and the tools the grant enables; a person at the L3 gate who decides a parked draft; and an operator or auditor who must explain a past model call without reading a stored prompt. The SRO and the Architecture Board read the outcome, not the run.

## Stories

- As a tenant admin, I want to author a recipe with section kinds, selectors and a character ceiling and activate an immutable version, so that the prompt a run compiles is a governed instrument rather than a template edited in place.
- As an internal agent, I want exactly the procedure, capability and role, knowledge, memory and card sources this step needs, in trust order, so that the instruction block cannot be preceded by tenant-supplied text.
- As a person at the L3 gate, I want to decide a parked draft and have the resume apply it without another model call, so that generated content reaches a card only through a decision that names it.
- As an auditor, I want each recorded call to carry its recipe pin and a 64-hex hash, so that I can move from a finding to the call and to the text it was found against.

## Scenarios

S1 a required procedure with no source refuses by name before a model call. S2 the same recipe and facts compile byte-identically. S3 a card change moves the hash and another tenant's card does not. S4 an over-budget section refuses with its measured size. S5 the audit names `(prompt_ref, prompt_sha256)`. S6 a handover parks the run and a person's approval applies the draft. S7 `cards.assign` writes the binding, the note and the bound run in one transaction. S8 a release with an unresolved required kind refuses `409 release_not_ready`.

## Verify

The offline check is `python3 scripts/rework-content-check.py --project S21 --content docs/evidence/rework/tranche-9/rework-content-S21.json --snapshot /tmp/snap-9/data --wsjf 9,6,7,8 --closes true`, followed by the factory run and its receipt assertion. The product half is the suites the plan names — prompt compile and catalogue, recipes, memory and knowledge, the executor and internal-agent runtimes, draft apply, card binding, run memory, card handoff, the decision ladder, ladder laya and organisation — read at the pinned snapshot; the live wire proof remains blocked on the licensed caller.

# Definition of ready — S21 Message construction (retrospective, Phase G)

## Independent

The pack writes only S21's record rows against the pinned 2026-11-28 snapshot; its product is in the tree and its units are the pack, its receipt and the close-gate documents, not a rebuild. No other member's act depends on this pack, and the pack depends on no member's act: the other tranche-9 packs share the snapshot and the cadence, but not a row S21 writes. Independence is therefore about the record, not about the programme calendar.

## Negotiable

The pack supplies the lifecycle set the standard binds — charter, baseline, contract, review, the Phase A–D artefacts and the close-gate document set of eight authored documents plus the artefact index — while the tranche review and production promotion belong to other roles. What is not negotiable is the honesty of the record: the live proof is recorded blocked, the tranche authorisation is escalated rather than assumed, and no green product gate is claimed. The scope of the pack can be refined; its evidence standard cannot.

## Valuable

The benefit is B1: every model call is explicable without storing the prompt text, because the recipe pin, the source identities and the SHA-256 make a past call reproducible and the audit names `(prompt_ref, prompt_sha256)`. A reviewer can move from a finding to the call and to the text it was found against, and the prompt is not a second data store to secure. The pack is what lets the tranche review read that benefit from a record rather than from a claim.

## Estimable

At the snapshot the project carries eleven open packages, three P1 and eight P2, and the WSJF inputs recorded by the tranche-9 PI plan are business value 9, time criticality 6, risk reduction 7 and job size 8. The factory journals every act, so an interrupted run resumes at the member it stopped on, and each package maps to a row this pack or its receipt supplies or explicitly escalates. The estimate is the package count, not a guess at effort.

## Small

One pack, one factory run, one receipt and one close-gate document set; no product rebuild, no migration, no cluster change and no service deploy. The unit is one branch and one pull request on the issue lane, and the pack's own content is the deliverable. Anything larger — a second prompt surface, a live wire run, a tranche authorisation — is out of this unit by construction.

## Testable

Every claim has an executable check: the offline content checker at the pinned snapshot, the factory's post-write receipt with one row per manifest check, the close-gate document set the standard requires, and the tranche exit gate that refuses a stale or red receipt. The audit half of the gate is the one claim whose evidence is stated rather than assumed: the review evidence records that no audit suite in the tree at 2026-11-28 asserts the `(prompt_ref, prompt_sha256)` pair, instead of naming one.

## Dependencies

The plan declares S09, S11, S13, S15, S16, T2 and T13 as upstream: retrieval and strata packs, procedure and step rows, the `agent.run` surface, the capability and knowledge tables, the prompt audit, and the release and executor contract. The project row records the same edges, and every S21 linked issue is closed at the snapshot. The executor budget mechanism is out of every S21 step and arrives from another lane; the live proof depends on the owner's licensed caller, which is a provisioning act, not a build.

documents.body:
# Definition of done — S21 Message construction (retrospective, Phase G)

## Acceptance criteria

The manifest `acceptance/programme/S21.toml` is the acceptance of record, with the plan's §9 as its content: a required source refuses by name; equal facts compile byte-identically; the card moves the hash and another tenant's card does not; an over-budget section refuses with its measurement; and the audit names `(prompt_ref, prompt_sha256)`. Each of the eleven open packages maps to a row the pack or its receipt supplies, or to an explicit escalation for the tranche authorisation that no content file can grant.

## Evidence at completion

The receipt is the evidence: one row per manifest check at the pinned snapshot, the content checker's verdict over this pack, the factory's post-write record and the transcript of the acts. The pack also carries the close-gate document set of eight authored documents plus the artefact index, the charter, baseline, contract and review, and the ten step receipts the plan names. The live wire proof is recorded blocked on the licensed caller rather than met, and the review evidence records the absent audit suite for the pair rather than asserting one.

## Repo gate

The change is docs-only: the design gates (`build-docs.py --check`, `check-docs.cjs`, `check-data.cjs`) and `git diff --check` run locally, and the repository's GitHub-hosted preflight plus the PR's CI are the compile, lint and final gates at the exact head. No local compiling cargo is run, and every filtered test is named by exact name before it is invoked, because a filter that selects zero tests exits zero and would read as a pass.

## Merge and closure

One pull request on the issue lane carries the pack, its receipt and the close-gate set, and it merges only after the content check and the local gate are green. The project does not close here: the manifest declares no closure checks and the record stays active, so closure is a later decision with a distinct approver. The tranche-9 authorisation remains the sponsoring group's or the programme owner's decision, and the pack ends by naming it rather than by assuming it.

risk.title: A second prompt path could quietly drift from the one compiler
risk.body: The plan forbids a second prompt compiler and PDDL as storage (§6, §12, §23), but the executor, the audit and any future action all need a compiled prompt. The risk is a later unit reconstructing the message in its own code and recording a hash that covers a different text. The defence the plan builds is one `prompt::compile` and one retrieval path, with the compiled text never stored and every recorded call naming `(prompt_ref, prompt_sha256)`. The risk is recorded so the review checks the new surface against the one compiler rather than trusting intent.
risk.response: Refuse any new surface that builds a prompt, and read every new action's prompt identity against the one compiler in review; the hash on `inference_call` is the evidence.

risk.title: The live wire proof is blocked on the estate's licensed caller
risk.body: Step 6's live proof (§17 P3) and step 11's P5 drive a bound run against the real inference-router and the real laya bridge, and a stub is explicitly not the proof. The plan records the live proof as blocked on the estate's caller licence, and the executor's gate records `gate_unavailable` when the tenant has no sealed laya token. Until the owner provisions a licensed test caller, the product's live evidence is absent even though every suite is green; the receipt must name the exact refusal rather than imply a live run.
risk.response: Provision the licensed caller, run the two ignored proofs, and record either the measured rows or the exact refusal in the receipt; never substitute a stub.

risk.title: Tenant-authored recipes widen the authoring and audit surface
risk.body: The recipe CRUD surface lets a tenant admin create a draft, activate it and retire the previous version. That is the decided shape (ADR 0009), with an edit being a new version and the audit being the existing `action_invocation` row. The risk is that a tenant-authored recipe changes the compiled prompt's trust order or budget in a way the audit only sees after a call. The plan mitigates it with the trust sort inside the compiler, the measured budget refusal, and one active version per key; the review should confirm the tenant path cannot bypass the compiler's ordering.
risk.response: Hold the compiler's trust sort and budget refusal as the invariant every recipe passes, and check the audit record for each activation of a tenant-authored version.

issue.title: The record carried no charter, baseline, artefact set, contract or Phase-G review
issue.body: At the 2026-11-28 snapshot the project row is active with the slice plan status built, and the audit carries the three P1 packages `project_in_unauthorised_tranche:S21`, `unpublished_declared_output:S21` and `mandatory_artefacts:S21`, and the P2 `wbs_absent:S21`. This pack supplies that lifecycle set retrospectively and records the product's build gate as the plan's and the manifest's, not as this pack's claim.
issue.response: Supplied by this pack and read off the project's receipt at the pinned snapshot; the product gate stays the build lane's.

issue.title: Two declared outputs were unpublished and the project had no WBS node
issue.body: The project-scoped register carries `unpublished_declared_output:S21` and `wbs_absent:S21`: it declares the `project-brief` and `evidence` outputs it has not published and has no WBS node. The pack's `project_brief_output` and `evidence_output` are the two declared outputs, and the `wbs_deliverable` row is the missing node with its four typed WSJF inputs 9, 6, 7 and 8 recorded by the tranche-9 PI plan.
issue.response: The two declared outputs and the WBS deliverable are authored here; the findings clear on the receipt rather than on an allowlist edit.

issue.title: The tranche itself has no authorisation, which no content pack can supply
issue.body: `project_in_unauthorised_tranche:S21` records that the project is active in tranche 9 while that tranche is still being prepared. This is a programme-level authorisation question: only the sponsoring group's or the programme owner's gate decision can authorise or re-plan the tranche, and a pack that wrote its own authorisation would be exactly the failure the audit exists to catch. The issue is recorded so the tranche review sees it rather than reading the pack as authority.
issue.response: Escalate to the programme owner with this pack's receipt; the tranche state is changed by their decision, never by a content file.

assumption.title: The 2026-11-28 tranche-9 snapshot is the authoritative record for S21
assumption.body: Every judgement in this pack is read from the pinned snapshot, and the content checker refuses any identifier that appears nowhere in it. The project row, its dependency edges, the nine linked issues and the plan status are read there; a row that changes when the build lane or the registry refresh merges is out of scope until the pack is re-preflighted, which is why the pack quotes the snapshot rather than the live service.

assumption.title: The upstream members supply the primitives the plan lists as existing
assumption.body: The plan's starting state treats S15's capability and knowledge rows, S16's prompt audit, S13's `agent.run`, S11's procedure steps and S09's `retrieval.query` and `strata` packs as present, and the project row records those edges as needs. The assumption is that their behaviour at the same snapshot still matches what the plan read; each build record re-checks the seam it extends, so a drift would surface as a red suite rather than as a silent fallback.

assumption.title: A person decides the L3 gate and a machine cannot sign it
assumption.body: The applying gate treats an `executor` approval as a person's act: the approval writer enforces `decided_by_kind = human`, `ladder.record` accepts `rung=human` only from a person citing an approved approval, and `ladder.apply_draft` admits only an accepted decision whose meta names the draft. The assumption is that the approval primitive keeps that enforcement; if a machine could decide the gate, the draft-apply guard would rest on the same forgeable surface the plan closes.

dependency.title: S21 depends on S09, S11, S13, S15, S16, T2 and T13
dependency.body: The slice plan's frontmatter declares depends_on S09, S11, S13, S15, S16, T2 and T13, and the project row records the same edges. S09 supplies the retrieval and strata packs the knowledge section queries, S11 the procedure and step rows the Request source renders, S13 the `agent.run` surface the executor extends, S15 the capability and knowledge tables, S16 the prompt audit that names the compiled text, and T2 and T13 the release and executor contract the runtime dispatches on.

dependency.title: The executor budget mechanism is the #526 lane's, not S21's
dependency.body: The plan puts the budget mechanism `v1-p75-1` outside every S21 step (steps 6, 9, 10 and 11 name it out of scope), because it is already resolved on the #526 lane with a tool-budget test binary and a `422 budget_missing` precheck. S21's runs therefore invoke tools under a spend gate that arrives from that lane; a second gate inside S21 would duplicate the mechanism, so the dependency is carried as a block on #526's delivery rather than as related work.

dependency.title: The live proof needs a licensed caller and a reachable router and laya bridge
dependency.body: The live wire proof in step 6 and step 11's P5 require the estate's real inference-router and the real laya bridge plus a sealed caller licence; the receipt records the proof as blocked on that caller. The dependency is on the owner's provisioning act, and it is the only item that keeps the product's live evidence open while every suite is green. A stub is refused by the test itself, so the gap cannot be papered over.

benefit.title: Every model call is explicable without storing the prompt text
benefit.body: The recipe pin, the section source identities and the SHA-256 of the compiled text make a past call reproducible without keeping the text: `inference_call` names `prompt_ref`, `prompt_version` and `prompt_sha256`, and an audit finding names the same pair. The benefit is that the prompt is not a second data store to secure and cannot drift from the call it produced, and a reviewer can move from a finding to the call to the text it was found against.

benefit.title: Context engineering replaces a fixed template and refuses rather than hides
benefit.body: The selector chooses the smallest set of sources that makes this step decidable, renders them in trust order and measures every section against its ceiling. The failure the plan names is not a missing section but a present, long, irrelevant one that costs tokens and hides the fact that mattered. The benefit is a compiled prompt whose composition is chosen at run time, whose over-budget case is a refusal with the measurement, and whose trust order keeps tenant text after the instructions.

benefit.title: A generated draft reaches a card only through a decision that names it
benefit.body: The plan closes the forgeable gate (`v1-w1c-2`): `ladder.apply_draft` admits only an accepted non-rule decision of `gate.precheck` or `gate.draft_apply` whose meta names the draft, the handover parks the run instead of failing it, and `documents.update` stays closed to generated drafts. The benefit is a structural property — a machine cannot attach generated content to a card without a recorded decision, and a person's approval is the one L3 path.

benefit.title: One retrieval path keeps knowledge pinned and out of the compile transaction
benefit.body: `crates/actions/src/knowledge/retrieval.rs` is extracted as the one retrieval implementation and reused by `knowledge.query`; `compile_for_run` resolves its targets in the transaction, commits, and calls retrieval with no transaction open. Pinned packs stay pinned and a missing or failed required pack keeps the existing `409 knowledge_degraded` semantics. The benefit is that the knowledge half of the prompt cannot diverge between the query action and the compiler, and a slow retrieval cannot hold a transaction.

body.commitments: S21 delivers message construction as product rows: the five tables and their migrations; the recipe, handoff, ladder, option and organisation-layer actions; the prompt, memory, knowledge and executor modules; and eleven build steps whose suites and receipts the plan names. It commits to one compiler for every source, one retrieval path outside any transaction, one executor dispatch point over a typed release anatomy, the compiled text never stored, budgets measured in characters with a refusal at the boundary, memory selection with its ids inside the hash, and a generated draft applying only through a decision that names it.
body.compliance: Compliance is demonstrated by `acceptance/programme/S21.toml` and the plan's §9 acceptance: a required source refusing by name before a model call, byte-identical compile on equal facts, the card's hash independence across tenants, the measured over-budget refusal, and the audit naming `(prompt_ref, prompt_sha256)`, with the pair itself still a design claim: no suite in the tree at 2026-11-28 asserts it (`crates/actions/tests/prompt_audits.rs` asserts `prompt_ref` only). project_brief_output:
# Project Brief — S21 Message Construction (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Outcome

Every model call carries a compiled prompt the run selected for this step: the procedure, the capability and its role, pinned knowledge, the run's prior steps and the card's memory, the declared request and the card's data, rendered in trust order with a recipe pin and a 64-hex SHA-256 recorded. A generated draft reaches a card only through an L1 laya decision or an L3 human approval that names it, and a release compiles its knowledge layers or refuses. The owner ruling of 2026-11-09 sets the frame: a prompt is a run-time compilation stored in Postgres, not a template.

## Boundary

S21 owns the compiler, the recipe lifecycle, the executor runtime's message half, the applied-draft gate, the memory selection and the release's knowledge layers. It does not own a second compiler, PDDL as storage, an external runtime, the executor budget mechanism (the #526 lane's `v1-p75-1`), any UI, parent-run memory in a child's prompt, a claim or lane verb, or the programme record. The judge's SOP document stays in the process judge; laya is not a prompt source.

## Reuse sources

The plan names S15's capability and knowledge tables, S16's prompt audit, S13's `agent.run`, S11's procedure steps and S09's `retrieval.query` and `strata` packs as the seams it extends. Inside the tree it reuses `prompt` and `prompt_section` from migration 0030, the pure renderer in `conveyor_domain::prompt`, the T0 executor contract and the #556/#568 bound-tool projection, and the existing approval and job primitives rather than adding a parallel escalation or queue.

## Inception units

Eleven build steps: budgets and the role component; the plan projection and declared step outputs; the work-package prompt envelope (#15); the `internal_agent` executor runtime and its tool grant (#581); the applying gate (#590); the work package's run (#599); the run's episodic memory (#612); the Request source (#624); the handoff (#649); the L1 laya gate (#656); and the level closing — apply on accept, prompt_ref required, the authorable ceiling and the release layers (#697). Each step names its suites and its receipt.

## Dependencies

The project's recorded dependencies are S09, S11, S13, S15, S16, T2 and T13. All nine linked issues (#15, #581, #590, #599, #612, #624, #649, #656, #697) are closed at the snapshot. The budget mechanism is the #526 lane's and is not carried here. The live wire proof depends on an owner-provisioned licensed caller and reachable inference-router and laya bridge, and the receipt records the proof as blocked on that caller.

## Acceptance

`acceptance/programme/S21.toml` carries the project-level acceptance, and the plan's §9 is its content: a required source refuses by name before a model call; equal facts compile byte-identically; the card moves the hash and another tenant's card does not; an over-budget section refuses with its measured size; and the audit names `(prompt_ref, prompt_sha256)`. Each step's build record adds its measured suites and reversal proofs; a green product gate at this snapshot is the build lane's to report, not this pack's to claim.

## Capabilities

Six. Author the recipe: a tenant admin creates a draft with sections, selectors and a ceiling, and activates or retires versions. Compile the request: the run's sources become one hashed prompt in trust order. Execute the work package: one step under the release anatomy with a closed grant. Gate and apply: L1 or L3 decides and the one helper applies. Hand off the card: binding, note as memory and the bound run in one transaction. Pin the release: typed grants and compiled knowledge layers.

## Plan

The plan is `docs/plans/slices/S21-message-construction.md`, status built, with its §10–§23 build records and the receipts `docs/evidence/S21-PLAN.md`, `S21-WORKPACKAGE.md`, `S21-EXECUTOR.md`, `S21-APPLY.md`, `S21-RUN.md`, `S21-MEMORY.md`, `S21-REQUEST.md`, `S21-HANDOFF.md`, `S21-LAYA.md` and `S21-EXECUTION.md`. The project stays active: this brief accompanies the record set and the two declared outputs and does not close the project.

# Evidence — S21 Message Construction (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

## Claim

S21 delivers the compiled prompt as product rows: recipe authoring with draft and active versions; a selector over kinds, limits and the knowledge query; one compiler that renders every source in trust order, measures budgets and hashes the text without storing it; an `internal_agent` executor that dispatches on the release anatomy under a closed tool grant; an L1 laya gate that makes and verifies its own call; an L3 human gate that applies a draft and a resume worker that never calls the model; memory that carries prior steps and the handoff note; and a release that compiles its knowledge layers or refuses.

## Evidence

`acceptance/programme/S21.toml` is the manifest of record. The plan's build records name the measured suites — `prompt_compile` 7/7, store `prompt_catalogue` 5, `prompt_recipes` 7/7, domain `prompt_memory` 8, `prompt_knowledge` 4/4, store `memory` 4, `executor_runtime` 5/5, `internal_agent_runtime` 16 with two ignored live proofs, `draft_apply` 7, `card_binding`, `run_memory`, `card_handoff`, `decision_ladder` 7, `organisation` — with reversal proofs fired and reverted for each. The migrations are 0030, 0031, 0032, 0062, 0071 and 0074; the receipts are `docs/evidence/S21-PLAN.md`, `S21-WORKPACKAGE.md`, `S21-EXECUTOR.md`, `S21-APPLY.md`, `S21-RUN.md`, `S21-MEMORY.md`, `S21-REQUEST.md`, `S21-HANDOFF.md`, `S21-LAYA.md`, `S21-EXECUTION.md` and `T0-RELEASE-LAYERS.md`.

## Verification

The manifest is read at the pinned snapshot through the programme record, and this Phase-G review reads the same receipt. The plan's rbuild lines are the historical gate: since the 2026-11-20 owner direction retired local compilation, the compile and lint verdict comes from the repository's GitHub-hosted preflight and the PR's CI, with `cargo-guard.py` on m4 only for interactive work. Every libtest filter is listed by exact name first, because a filter that selects zero tests exits zero and would read as a pass, and a piped command's exit status is the pipeline's, so the gate log is captured to a file.

## Links
The source of truth is `docs/plans/slices/S21-message-construction.md`; the acceptance is `acceptance/programme/S21.toml`; the artefact set is indexed by the architecture-artifact document in this pack; the decisions are ADR 0009 (prompt selection and recipe authoring), ADR 0015, ADR 0018, ADR 0019 and ADR 0020. The project stays active and this pack does not close it.
